 Our operations are affected by seasonal trends typical in the outdoor apparel and footwear industry and have historically resulted in higher sales and profits in the third and fourth calendar quarters. This pattern has resulted primarily from the timing of shipments of fall season products to wholesale customers in the third and fourth quarters and proportionally higher sales in our direct-to-consumer operations in the fourth quarter, combined with an expense base that is more consistent throughout the year. We believe that our liquidity requirements for at least the next 12 months will be adequately covered by existing cash, cash provided by operations and existing short-term borrowing arrangements.

attrs.management_says: Revenue growth driven by underlying demand drivers.
attrs.numbers_show: Quarterly receivables signals show disproportionate AR buildup in H2: Q3 AR +15.5% vs revenue +13.7% (DSO 62→63), Q4 AR +8.0% vs revenue +3.3% (DSO 46→48). This pattern is consistent with seasonal fall wholesale shipment timing (channel loading) rather than pure demand growth. H2 contributed ~$115M (51%) of the full-year revenue increase.
attrs.verdict: explanation does not fit the numbers

attrs.management_says: No explicit explanation for 2015 receivables movement in evidence; general references to seasonality and ERP implementation (E30, E49).
attrs.numbers_show: Receivables grew 8.0% ($27.6M) vs revenue +10.7%; DSO improved from 60 to 58 days (E23). Quarterly: Q1 AR +1% (DSO 53→48), Q2 AR -3% (DSO 57→47), Q3 AR +15.5% (DSO 62→63), Q4 AR +8% (DSO 46→48) (E25-E28). Pattern shows AR growing slower than revenue overall, consistent with healthy demand.

attrs.reason: Operating cash flow fell 49% (E6, E17, E24) while net income rose 27%; the provided MD&A excerpts (E30, E47, E49) do not quantify working capital movements (inventory, payables) or ERP cash outflows to explain the divergence.

rebuttal.innocent_explanation: The 49% decline in operating cash flow despite higher net income reflects a substantial inventory build to support the 13.7% Q3 revenue surge and fall seasonal shipments (E27, E49), compounded by cash outflows from the May 2015 ERP implementation in international distributor businesses (E30).

attrs.final_verdict: explanation does not fit the numbers
